title: Strict JSON decoding and structural schema boundary

claims.text: strict_loads rejects duplicate keys, non-finite numbers, non-JSON types, invalid unicode and container cycles before any schema assertion runs.
validate preflights the complete schema with _schema_node, checks the instance with _check_json, then applies conjunctive assertions in fixed keyword order.
_assertions enforces enum and const with JSON equality that treats bool as a distinct type from numbers, matching the safe-integer and nesting limits.
SchemaError carries code bad_args with independent instance pointer and schema pointer, so failures report exactly where the instance or the schema is wrong.

decision.rule: Change here when strict decoding, schema preflight, assertion order or equality semantics need to change.
decision.failure: An invalid JSON value passes decoding, a bool is accepted as an integer, or a schema keyword is silently ignored.

questions.q: Where does strict_loads reject duplicate keys and non-finite numbers?
Where should I change the assertion order in _assertions?
Where can I debug a schema failure from its instance and schema pointers?
How does validate distinguish invalid_schema from instance failures?
